description_text:
AI Job Summary

* Willingness to learn and develop practical AI capability, including using approved AI tools confidently and responsibly.
* Ability to turn ideas into practical AI-enabled processes, workflows, prototypes, agents, and tools.
* Clear communication skills to explain AI opportunities and concepts in business language to stakeholders.

Sign up or log in to analyse my fit

### **Role Type**

Within Australia • Contract • Full-time • Internship

### **Description**

**Start your career solving real problems and shaping better ways of working**

Hampshire is looking for curious, commercially minded graduates who want to help shape how a growing Australia and New Zealand business works with AI. This is not a traditional graduate program. You will learn about our business from the ground up, work across operational and corporate environments, and help turn genuine business problems into practical AI-enabled processes, workflows, prototypes, agents and tools.

Through structured AI development, meaningful rotations and exposure to experienced leaders, you will build the commercial, operational and leadership capability to become a future manager and an AI advocate across Hampshire. You do not need to begin as an AI expert, but you do need to be curious, proactive and excited about using emerging technology to create measurable improvements.

**Opportunities in this stream**

This stream offers five graduate opportunities for curious, AI-savvy graduates from any degree background. When you apply, tell us which areas interest you most.

* **AI:** getting stuck into AI projects with our Capability team and finding better ways to do things across the business.
* **Design:** design work alongside our Head of Design. SketchUp skills are an advantage.
* **Revenue:** supporting the commercial work that helps our business grow, from pricing and partnerships to digital channels and guest insights, and helping deliver revenue improvements across the business.
* **IT:** helping plan, track and deliver technology projects across the business.
* **New Zealand business unit:** solving real problems for our New Zealand business using AI, data and simple tools, with occasional travel to New Zealand.

**Please note:** The New Zealand business unit role is based in Australia, and you must be willing to work New Zealand business hours.

**What you will experience**

During the 12-month program, you will:

* Join a home business unit or Shared Services function.
* Complete meaningful rotations based on business priorities and development opportunities.
* Learn from operational teams and the people closest to the work.
* Investigate processes, pain points and opportunities for improvement.
* Use approved AI tools to research, analyse and test ideas.
* Help develop prototypes and beta test potential solutions.
* Support teams to implement practical improvements.
* Participate in regular AI learning and collaborative problem-solving sessions.
* Work with other graduates on genuine Hampshire business challenges.
* Build relationships with leaders and teams across Hampshire.

You will be supported by a Graduate Manager, buddy, Graduate Program Lead and the wider graduate cohort.

**Build practical AI capability**

You do not need to join Hampshire as an AI expert.

We are looking for people who are interested in technology, willing to learn and curious about how AI could improve the way a business operates.

As part of the program, you will receive structured AI development and opportunities to apply your learning to real work. You will learn how to:

* Use approved AI tools confidently and responsibly.
* Understand a business problem before choosing a solution.
* Map and analyse processes.
* Identify repetitive or low-value work.
* Develop and test practical ideas.
* Consider privacy, cybersecurity, data and implementation risks.
* Explain AI opportunities in clear business language.
* Share learning and help others build confidence.

Our goal is to develop graduates who can become practical AI advocates across Hampshire.

**Who we are looking for**

You do not need to be an AI expert or come from a technology degree. We are looking for high-potential graduates and early-career candidates who are genuinely excited by the opportunity to use AI, technology and fresh thinking to improve how a business operates.

You may be a good fit if you:

* Actively explore AI, emerging technology or new digital tools.
* Are commercially curious and want to understand how a business works.
* Enjoy investigating complex or unclear problems and finding practical solutions.
* Can turn an idea into action rather than stopping at the concept stage.
* Take ownership, show initiative and are comfortable working with limited direction.
* Think critically, challenge assumptions respectfully and ask thoughtful questions.
* Communicate clearly with operational teams, technical specialists and business leaders.
* Consider the people, risks and practical realities involved in implementing change.
* Are willing to spend time in our operations and learn from the people closest to the work.
* Want to develop into a future manager or leader with strong commercial and AI capability.

A degree in any discipline is welcome but not essential for these roles. We are looking for people who are curious, keen to learn and comfortable using AI. An analytics, business, IT or data background is an advantage for the New Zealand role.

**What matters to us**

Our values will shape how graduates learn, contribute and work with others:

**Care:** Listen, collaborate and understand the needs of our people, residents, guests and business.

**Courage:** Ask questions, challenge established ways of working and put forward thoughtful ideas.

**Innovation:** Use AI, technology and fresh thinking to develop practical improvements.

**About Hampshire**

Hampshire is a family-owned business operating residential communities, holiday parks and long-stay accommodation across Australia and New Zealand.

Our business is diverse, practical and connected to the everyday experiences of our residents, guests and employees. As a Hampshire graduate, you will have the opportunity to understand the business from the ground up and contribute to work with a visible purpose.

**Application process**

Our recruitment process is designed to understand your potential, motivation and approach to learning.

It is expected to include:

* A short online application
* A recorded digital interview
* A conversation with Hampshire
* A practical business activity
* Reference and eligibility checks

We are interested in how you think and learn, not polished corporate answers or advanced knowledge of AI.

**Program details**

**Program commencement:** Monday 8 February 2027

**Program duration:** 12 months

**Applications open:** 6 October 2026

**Applications close:** 29 October 2026

**Locations and work arrangements:** Remote. We will only consider candidates based in Sydney, Melbourne or Brisbane.

**Operational exposure:** Travel to Hampshire sites will be required

**New Zealand business unit role:** must be willing to work New Zealand business hours.

**Ready to get involved**

If you are curious, ready to learn and interested in using AI to solve real business problems, we would love to hear from you.

Apply to join the Hampshire Graduate Program and help us explore better ways of working across our business.

Hampshire is committed to providing a fair and accessible recruitment experience. Please let us know if you require a reasonable adjustment or an alternative way to participate in any stage of the process.

Please note: Successful candidates will be required to complete a National Police Check as part of the pre-employment process [confirm].

**Company Overview**

Leveraging decades of experience, Equans Solar & Storage is the one-stop partner for scaled,
  
integrated and performant solutions on solar & storage energy projects.

  

**Our mission :** serving energy transition and low carbon world by empowering the deployment and
  
integration of solar and storage solutions.

  

We provide solar PV & hybrid plants, energy storage, innovation and solar PV B2B customers.

  

Operating in 15 countries, with more than 1,500 experts dedicated to solar PV and high voltage,
  
Equans Solar & Storage has installed over 6GW solar energy capacity worldwide, 550 MWh BESS
  
and is operating and maintaining approximately 2GW of solar PV plants.

  

Our Australian team consists of approximately 50 highly skilled engineers, and it is expanding
  
rapidly due to the growth of large-scale hybrid projects.

  

**Program Overview**

Equans Solar & Storage will imminently launch its Lightspeed Solar Portfolio (LSP) program, a
  
utility-scale testbed environment to trial and deploy innovation projects that help to lower the cost
  
of constructing and operating large-scale solar and storage projects. LSP will be part of ARENA’s
  
Advancing Renewables Program, contributing to ARENA’s goals to reduce LCOE of renewables
  
technologies in Australia.

  

**The team you’ll be joining**

Our Australian team consists of approximately 50 highly skilled engineers, and it is expanding
  
rapidly due to the growth of large-scale hybrid projects.
  
You will be a part of our growing Innovations team tasked with the implementation of our LSP
  
program, specifically in the Digital and Construction workstreams.

  

Want to learn more about our projects? Click here :
  
Solar & Storage Solutions for Energy Efficiency | Equans

What you’ll be leading
  
You’ll report to the Innovation leader, our key person in Australia managing the LSP program, and
  
will be working closely with our Civil team based in Sydney.

**Your rôle and responsibilities:**

* Primary role: Develop, refine and validate data analytics and machine learning models to

identify ground conditions associated with piling refusal on Equans current and future
  
solar and storage projects.
  

* Consolidate and manage large datasets from intrusive investigations (e.g. boreholes, test

pits), non-intrusive investigations (e.g. geophysical surveys), and piling installation records.
  

* Build predictive models and data visualization tools to improve ground risk assessment,

project budgeting and construction planning.
  

* Continue and enhance an existing preliminary model previously developed by Equans in

France, adapting it to Australian ground conditions and project requirements.
  

* Collaborate with engineering, construction and innovation teams to translate technical

findings into practical recommendations for project development and delivery.
  

* Prepare technical reports, presentations and documentation to communicate

methodologies, assumptions and key findings to internal stakeholders.
  

* Liaise with consultants, performing technical analysis of consultants proposals, attend site

visits/occasional travels to site

**The profile we’re looking for**

* Undergraduate in Data Science/AI/Computer Science or similar;
* Has preferably undertaken modules or has experience with geotechnical engineering,

geophysics, and/or civil engineering;
  

* Proficient in Python and common data science libraries
* Proactive, innovative, independent and curious

  

**Our recruitment process**  
1. An initial conversation with the recruiter/Local HR
  
2. One or two interviews with the hiring manager or relevant team lead
  
3. A final conversation may be held with an additional senior team member.

  

We’ll keep you informed every step of the way – our process is guided by transparency and care.

  

**Our Commitment**  
At Equans, we believe in the value of diverse talent. This role is open to all candidates, including
  
individuals with disabilities.
  
We are committed to fostering a culture of diversity, inclusion, and safety – key pillars of who we
  
are as a company.

* Sydney - Linfield
* Applications close 27 October
* The salary range for this role is $89,576 - $96,829

**About the Department**
------------------------

The Department of Industry, Science and Resources and our broader portfolio are integral to the Australian Government’s economic agenda. Our purpose is to help the government build a better future for all Australians through enabling a productive, resilient and sustainable economy, enriched by science and technology. We do this by:

* Growing innovative & competitive businesses, industries and regions
* Investing in science and technology
* Strengthening the resources sector.

The APS and the department offer a clear direction and meaningful work. You will be able to create positive impact in people’s lives whilst contributing to improved outcomes for Australia and our people.  
  
If you would like to feel a strong connection to your work and you are accountable, committed and open to change, join us in shaping Australia’s future.  
  
Please see the APSC’s APS Employee Value Proposition for more information on the benefits and value of employment within the APS.  

**About the team**
------------------

We are the Australian Government’s national authority on measurement.  
  
At the National Measurement Institute (NMI), we empower innovation and protect trust in Australian industry and society through world-class measurement science. Join a team where your expertise drives national impact, your curiosity is nurtured, and the work you do creates trusted measurement for a fair, safe, healthy and competitive Australia. Our employees enjoy career development opportunities, flexible working arrangements and the opportunity to shape Australia’s economic future through world-class measurement science.  
  
At NMI, precision meets purpose.  
  
We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive and impactful workplace by hiring people who share our values and bring integrity, collaboration and innovation to everything they do.  
  
The Physical Metrology Branch develops, maintains and disseminates Australia’s peak physical measurement standards. It provides traceability assurance so measurements made in Australia are accepted internationally. Branch staff deliver calibration and other measurement services, contribute to international measurement forums and share expertise with Australian and international stakeholders.  
  
The Mass and Density Standards team maintains Australia’s primary standards and deliver the nation’s highest-level calibration services from milligrams to tonnes. Its work supports calibration and testing laboratories and sectors including advanced manufacturing, biomedical, defence and aerospace. The team operates within an ISO/IEC 17025-accredited quality system, develops and validates primary standards and automated calibration systems, and is advancing a new density measurement facility and research into an electrostatic force balance for improved sub-milligram measurement.

**The opportunity**
-------------------

Start or build your scientific or engineering career at Australia’s national measurement authority. With structured training and support from experienced scientists and engineers, you will develop specialist capability in precision mass and density measurement while contributing to nationally significant calibration services and Australia’s primary measurement standards.

**What’s in it for you?**
-------------------------

Join a community of professionals committed to technical measurement excellence and cutting-edge research. We invest in advanced facilities, foster collaboration with leading institutions and support innovation. You will work with people who have diverse skill sets including scientists, engineers, policy specialists and regulatory professionals.  
  
This role offers an early-career scientist or engineer a strong technical foundation in measurement science. You will receive practical training and develop valuable, transferable skills in complex measurement systems, instrumentation, data acquisition, measurement uncertainty and laboratory quality systems.  
  
As part of the Department of Industry, Science and Resources, employees at NMI are covered by an enterprise agreement and benefits include:

* Parental leave
* a vacation care subsidy
* $235 annual healthy lifestyle subsidy
* access to study assistance
* access to Employee Assistance Program - health, wellbeing, counselling and support when needed

**Our ideal candidate**
-----------------------

We are seeking an early-career scientist or engineer who is curious, practical and motivated to build specialist expertise in mass and density metrology. The role may also suit a laboratory technician or metrologist with relevant experience. You do not need prior expertise in mass and density measurement. Structured training, supervision and support will be provided as you develop capability and independence.  
  
You will:

* Demonstrate sound technical judgement, strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.
* Show initiative, curiosity and a willingness to learn and develop specialist skills in mass measurement and laboratory operations.
* Be comfortable working in a structured laboratory environment and applying quality, safety and accreditation requirements.
* Analyse technical information and data to solve problems, investigate issues and support evidence-based decisions.
* Take responsibility for delivering quality outcomes and maintaining the integrity of your work.
* Build productive working relationships and communicate technical information effectively.
* Work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
* Hold a tertiary qualification in physics, engineering or a related discipline, or have equivalent relevant laboratory experience.
* Experience with laboratory instrumentation, automation, programming or data acquisition systems such as Python, VBA or LabVIEW will be highly regarded.

We are looking for individuals who bring personal integrity and a sense of purpose, and who embody NMI's values of being Inclusive, Innovative, Accountable, Adaptable, Influential and Strategic.  
  
Our department has a commitment to inclusion and diversity, with an ambition of being the best possible place to work. This reflects the importance we place on our people and on creating a workplace culture where each and every one of us is valued and respected for our contribution. Our ideal candidate adds to this culture and our workplace in their own way.

**What you will do**
--------------------

Following training and working under limited direction within established laboratory, quality and safety frameworks, you will apply and continue to develop your professional and technical expertise to:

* Deliver timely, high-quality calibrations of weights, balances and hydrometers, and measurements of liquid and solid density and surface tension, using methods that support internationally recognised levels of accuracy.
* Plan and manage assigned calibration workflows, liaise with clients and resolve routine technical or scheduling issues to meet service agreements.
* Analyse measurement data, calculate and propagate uncertainty, interpret results and prepare clear technical records, reports and calibration documentation.
* Monitor equipment status, arrange calibrations and maintenance, and keep laboratory records accurate and current.
* Apply the ISO/IEC 17025 quality system and contribute to method documentation, validation, corrective action and continuous improvement.
* Investigate technical issues, diagnose equipment or process faults, and recommend and implement practical solutions within delegated authority.
* Contribute to the design, development and validation of new standards facilities, automated calibration systems and improvements to existing measurement systems.
* Contribute technical knowledge to team research and development activities, share information and adapt priorities to meet evolving client and business needs.

NMI values continuous learning and is committed to supporting staff to reach their full potential. In this role, you will have the opportunity to:

* Gain hands-on experience in a highly specialised and nationally significant area of measurement science, developing expertise in mass and density metrology through the calibration of weights, balances and hydrometers, and the measurement of liquid and solid density and surface tension.
* Build expertise in measurement uncertainty, traceability and quality systems within an ISO 17025-accredited laboratory.
* Apply your science or engineering skills to solve real-world measurement challenges across a range of industries.
* Collaborate with experienced scientists, engineers and metrologists on research and capability development projects that support Australia's national measurement infrastructure.

**Eligibility**
---------------

A tertiary qualification in physics, engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant laboratory experience, is required.

To be eligible for employment in the APS and the department, candidates must be Australian Citizens.  
  
Positions require a Baseline security clearance and successful candidates will be required to obtain and maintain a clearance at this level.

**Notes**
---------

A merit pool may be established and used to fill future vacancies within 18 months from the date the vacancy was first advertised in the Gazette.  
  
The department does currently offer flexible work opportunities for many roles. This is a Sydney-based laboratory role. Flexible work arrangements may be considered where they are compatible with operational and laboratory requirements. Please contact the contact officer to discuss this further.

**Application information**
---------------------------

Your application must not contain any classified or sensitive information. This includes in your application responses, CV and any other documents. The selection panel may not consider applications containing classified information.  
  
Please provide a pitch explaining how your skills, knowledge and experience will be relevant to this role and why you are the best candidate for the position. Your pitch can contain no more than 750 words and should align to the key duties listed above.  
  
You may use AI tools to support your application. However, all content must be accurate, authentic, and reflect your own capability in line with APS merit principles. For further guidance, please refer to the APSC’s Principles for candidate use of AI in recruitment.  
  
Please complete your application online and provide your current CV with your application. (CVs must be in .doc, .docx, or .pdf format).  
  
Accessible application documentation is available in other formats on request. Please contact recruitment@industry.gov.au or (02) 6276 1235 if you require assistance with your application.  
  
Please refer to our Applying for a position information for additional information on how to apply.

-----------------------

For more information regarding this opportunity, please contact Kitty Fen on +612 84673519 or via email on kitty.fen@measurement.gov.au

* Responsible Person

* Educational Leader

This role is responsible for overseeing the cinematic vision and visual storytelling of the film through a lighting lens. The Head of Cinematography, Lighting works inside of NAS to lead the Lighting department and ensure the visual quality, consistency, and continuity of lighting across the production, shaping mood, atmosphere, and readability in every shot.

* Lead and mentor Lighting Supervisors, Leads, and Artists, setting expectations and providing creative and technical feedback in dailies and reviews
* Review and approve lighting work, maintaining continuity and quality standards across sequences and shots
* Partner with Modeling, Surfacing, Environments, FX, CFX, and Compositing to ensure seamless integration of assets and effects into final lit and composited images
* Oversee the creation and maintenance of lighting rigs, templates, and workflows that support efficiency and consistency across the show
* Collaborate with CG/Technical Supervisors, Production Technology, and R&D on pipeline developments, tool needs, and the technical feasibility of lighting concepts
* Troubleshoot and resolve escalated lighting-related technical issues with TDs and engineering partners
* Work closely with Production Management to bid, schedule, and track lighting work, ensuring milestones are met on time and within budget

description_text:
The Talent Acquisition Consultant (Visa and Relocation) delivers high quality end to end services and support to managers particularly in the recruitment of positions where the expected applicant is overseas or interstate.

* **Salary $125K - $140K per annum plus 17% superannuation**
* **Full-time continuing appointment**
* **Macquarie University, Wallumattagal Campus, North Ryde**

***Open the door for global talent – specialist immigration expertise that brings the world's best minds to Macquarie***

Every year, academics, researchers, clinicians and professional staff from around the world choose to build their careers at Macquarie University. Behind each of those arrivals sits a visa pathway to navigate, a nomination to lodge, a family to settle and a compliance obligation to meet. This is where you come in.

As our Visa, Relocation and Global Mobility Specialist, you will be the University's subject matter expert on immigration and mobility. You will advise hiring managers, faculty leadership and candidates on visa options and eligibility, manage the end-to-end visa lifecycle for international academics and researchers, and coordinate relocation arrangements that help new starters and their families settle in quickly. You will also safeguard the University's compliance position, maintaining sponsorship records, monitoring visa expiries and keeping us audit-ready.

Sitting within the Talent Acquisition team in Human Resources, this is a rare specialist role in a complex, highly regulated environment where your advice has visible impact on individual careers, on research programs, and on Macquarie's ability to attract the best talent globally. If you enjoy untangling intricate immigration matters and translating legislation into clear, practical guidance, you will find plenty of scope here.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Head of Talent Acquisition, you will provide specialist, high-level guidance, information, compliance oversight and reporting on immigration and relocation matters to internal stakeholders, current staff, prospective staff and international visitors.

Your responsibilities will include:

  

* Providing expert advice to hiring managers and University leaders on visa and immigration regulations, compliance and reporting
* Assessing visa eligibility, explaining visa subclasses (including 407, 408, 482 and 186) and outlining step-by-step processes for existing staff, prospective employees and visiting academics
* Managing the visa lifecycle for distinguished researchers and postdoctoral fellows, including employer nomination processing and correspondence with government departments
* Applying and upholding the University's immigration policies and procedures, mitigating risk across all cases and escalating any breaches
* Maintaining mandatory sponsorship records, tracking visa expiry dates and work right compliance and ensuring readiness for federal immigration audits
* Acting as the primary contact point between the University, external legal counsel and government departments, and liaising with external agencies to resolve issues as they arise
* Coordinating international and domestic relocation benefits, housing resources and onboarding logistics for incoming staff and their families
* Delivering information sessions and training to HR colleagues and stakeholders across the organisation on immigration changes, compliance, visa sponsorship and policy adherence

**About Us**

Human Resources sits within the portfolio of the Deputy Vice-Chancellor People and Operations, delivering high-level strategic advisory services to Macquarie University and its entities including Macquarie University Hospital and Health Clinics, and U@MQ, the University's commercial enterprise. Our HR Business Partnering teams and Centres of Expertise span Employee Relations, Talent Acquisition, Remuneration, and Capability, Culture and Inclusion, with HR Shared Services and HR Applications underpinning the portfolio.

The Talent Acquisition team is the specialist function responsible for attracting and acquiring domestic and international talent across the University and its entities. Our work is guided by Macquarie's values: collective ambition, purposeful collaboration, bold innovation and genuine care.

**About You (Selection Criteria)**

You are an immigration and mobility specialist who reads legislation closely, keeps meticulous records and explains complex requirements in plain language. You navigate large organisations with ease, handle sensitive personal information with discretion, and find practical solutions when a case does not fit the standard pathway.

  

* Qualifications in HR, business, law or a related discipline and/or substantial relevant experience; OMARA registration desirable
* Demonstrated experience in immigration consulting, corporate mobility or global relocation, ideally within a university, large public sector institution or comparable regulated environment
* Detailed knowledge of Australian immigration legislation and visa processes, including visa subclasses 407, 408, 482 and 186, academic exemptions and pathways relevant to research and higher education
* Proven expertise in employer-sponsored visas, nomination processing and immigration compliance, with the capability to interpret and apply migration legislation autonomously within a complex organisational context
* High-level stakeholder engagement skills, including liaison with government agencies, external legal counsel and senior University stakeholders, along with discretion in handling personal data
* Well-developed case management skills, exceptional attention to detail, and the capacity to organise multiple priorities within tight timelines
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience delivering information sessions or training on compliance-related matters

**How to Apply**

To be considered, please apply online with your CV and a cover letter outlining how your experience aligns with the selection criteria (above).

**Applications Close: 18 October 2026**

**We reserve the right to progress or decline an application prior to the application closing date.**

For enquiries, or a confidential conversation about the role please contact Sarah Bate, Head of Talent Acquisition at sarah.bate@mq.edu.au

**Why Join Us?**

Macquarie is a university engaged with the real and often complex problems and opportunities that define our lives. Since our foundation over 60 years ago, we have aspired to be a different type of university. Over the years, we have grown to become the centre of a vibrant local and global community. Connect with us today.

We rank amongst the top employers in the Australian Workplace Employers Index. Explore the fantastic benefits available to you when you become part of the team at Macquarie University.

  

* Flexible, hybrid work arrangements
* 17% Superannuation
* Subsidised onsite parking options
* Extensive training and professional development programs
* Onsite childcare facilities to support working parents
* Onsite vacation care during school holidays
* Discounted health insurance

* Access to an Employee Assistance Program for free and confidential support
* Convenient onsite GP, imaging, and physiotherapy clinics

Your employment is conditional upon the completion and maintenance of all role-required pre-employment or background checks in terms satisfactory to the University.

***This role requires a criminal history check. Australian citizenship or full working rights in Australia are required.***

Are you passionate about research and generating investment ideas? We’re looking for a professional to join our REITs sector team in Sydney, to develop valuable insights and investment ideas for our clients.

***Help unlock the biology of motor neurone disease and contribute to the search for new treatments***

Motor neurone disease (MND) remains one of the most complex challenges in neuroscience, and the laboratory work behind every discovery matters. As a Research Assistant in the Macquarie University Centre for Motor Neuron Disease, you will work at the bench alongside researchers investigating the cellular mechanisms and molecular pathways of neurodegeneration, and helping to evaluate new treatment strategies in cell and zebrafish models.

You will join a research community of more than 70 people focused on MND, with access to state-of-the-art facilities, advanced imaging and preclinical models, and an active Early Career Researcher network ('EnCouRage'). Reporting to Associate Professor Marco Morsch, you will be part of a team where technical care and curiosity are valued equally, and where your day-to-day contribution feeds directly into research with real human impact.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with hands-on molecular and cellular biology experience who would like to grow their research career within a recognised centre of excellence, with scope to develop new techniques, contribute to publications and build lasting research relationships across the University and beyond.

**About the Role**

Working under the direction of the principal researcher, you will provide practical research and laboratory assistance across a portfolio of MND projects. Your responsibilities will include:

  

* Providing research assistance to projects examining the molecular and cellular mechanisms of neurodegeneration in MND, in line with approved research protocols
* Undertaking and assisting with a range of cellular biology and preclinical research projects, including work in cell and zebrafish models
* Participating in, and assisting with, data management and analysis
* Updating and maintaining databases for project samples and research data
* Contributing to day-to-day laboratory management, including equipment, consumables and record keeping
* Building effective working relationships with a diverse range of researchers, professional staff and students
* Working in line with relevant EEO, WHS, biosafety and research ethics requirements

Please note that work hours may vary from time to time to accommodate operational needs.

**About Us**

Macquarie University's Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences builds on our aspiration to have the nation's first fully integrated Academic Health Sciences Centre under a university's leadership. It brings together the excellent work of medical and allied-health clinicians and researchers across the University and around the country, with unparalleled access to the world-leading clinical resources and research facilities found only on our campus.

The Centre for Motor Neuron Disease is well integrated into the Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences and the Department of Biomedical Sciences. The Centre has established state-of-the-art research facilities and offers outstanding development options, including an active Early Career Researcher support network ('EnCouRage'), within a team of more than 70 staff working on MND.

**About You**

You are a capable laboratory scientist who enjoys precise, methodical work and takes pride in reliable, well-documented results. You bring practical molecular and cellular biology skills, clear communication, and the organisational habits needed to keep multiple projects moving in a busy research environment.

**Selection Criteria**

  

* Bachelor degree or equivalent in medical science or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience
* Knowledge and understanding of cell biology, genetic and genomic analysis
* Experience with molecular and cellular biology techniques such as DNA/RNA purification, cell culture, fluorescent microscopy, western blotting and immunostaining
* Experience with molecular biology techniques such as DNA cloning (Gibson, Gateway), DNA construct assembly, PCR, gel electrophoresis and in vitro mRNA production
* Working knowledge of ethics and safe practice in a laboratory environment
* Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to liaise effectively with researchers, students and stakeholders
* Well-organised approach to work, with the ability to prioritise, manage multiple tasks and meet competing deadlines

**Desirable**

  

* Experience working with mice or zebrafish
* Experience with confocal microscopy and histology techniques

Macquarie University is transforming how it designs, delivers and assures the quality of its coursework suite. Sitting within the Curriculum Quality Unit in the Pro Vice-Chancellor (Education) portfolio, this position places you at the point where curriculum policy, education systems, data and day-to-day faculty practice meet.

As a Business Analyst, Curriculum, you will work within the PVCE portfolio, faculties and business teams to surface needs, examine processes and data, and translate what you find into practical solutions that improve services, efficiency and decision-making. You will produce clear documentation, facilitate stakeholder engagement and help ensure solutions align with strategy, governance and risk requirements.

We believe context makes the work meaningful. As the higher education sector continues to raise the bar on teaching quality, the systems that underpin the delivery, monitoring and evaluation of teaching need to be well-governed, fit for purpose and actively managed. Business analysis capability is central to navigating Macquarie's systemic landscape, progressing the transformation set out in the MQ Advantage Education Strategy, and responding to a moving technical and legislative environment.

If you enjoy untangling complexity and seeing your recommendations translated into real change for students and staff, this position offers genuine scope.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Curriculum Manager, you will develop and modify processes, systems and practices that can affect University-wide projects and improvement initiatives. Your responsibilities will include:

  

* Eliciting, examining and validating business needs, pain points and opportunities through workshops, interviews, process observation and data review.
* Mapping current and future processes, capabilities and customer journeys, and identifying gaps, risks and dependencies.
* Defining problem statements, benefits and success measures to inform prioritisation and business cases.
* Translating needs into clear business, functional and non-functional requirements with acceptance criteria and end-to-end traceability.
* Engaging stakeholders to build alignment, balance competing priorities, and communicate recommendations and artefacts.
* Assisting delivery through design clarification, solution option assessment, testing and UAT, go-live readiness, and change and training inputs, while meeting governance and compliance obligations across privacy, information management and security.
* Reviewing system data, configurations and workflows to identify issues, trends and opportunities for optimisation or standardisation across curriculum and education systems.
* Providing subject-matter input into system enhancements, integrations and upgrades, in line with enterprise architecture, governance and strategic priorities.
* Contributing curriculum analysis and knowledge of curriculum policy and practice, including impact analysis of proposed curriculum changes and oversight of teach-out arrangements and transitional provisions, in partnership with faculties.

**About us**

The Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic) portfolio is responsible for Macquarie's academic mission: the planning, quality and delivery of education for our undergraduate and graduate students, academic standards, student experience, and the governance frameworks behind learning and teaching.

Within the portfolio, the Pro Vice-Chancellor (Education) oversees education across the student journey, from pathways and access through to curriculum development and graduate outcomes. The Curriculum Quality Unit supports this work by applying the Curriculum Lifecycle Framework to maintain the quality of the University’s coursework programs.

Joining the team means playing a direct role in improving curriculum and strengthening the systems and data the University uses to understand and demonstrate the quality of its education.

**About You**

You are an experienced business analyst who reads complexity well: you can see how systems, data, processes and people fit together, and you can explain what you find in language that makes sense to everyone in the room. You are comfortable moving between detailed requirements work and bigger-picture advice, and you bring a methodical, evidence-based approach to improving how things work.

**Selection Criteria**

  

* A tertiary qualification in a relevant field (e.g. Information Systems, Education Technology, Business Analysis) or equivalent knowledge, skills and experience, with a demonstrated interest in ongoing professional development.
* Extensive relevant experience as an analyst in a complex environment, preferably an educational setting, with insight into how systems, data and processes interact.
* Knowledge of curriculum management systems, enterprise platforms or other complex business systems, including experience across process mapping, data interpretation, business intelligence and system optimisation.
* Proficiency with tools (e.g. Jira/Confluence, Miro, Visio, Excel/Power BI) and the ability to turn data and system behaviour into clear insights and recommendations.
* Demonstrated ability to interpret data, validate information, identify trends or issues, and apply insights to decision-making, prioritisation and solution design.
* Well-developed verbal, written and stakeholder communication skills, including facilitating workshops, balancing competing priorities and conveying complex information to audiences with varying levels of technical knowledge.
* Knowledge of higher education policy and legislation, and familiarity with educational systems and platforms. (Highly Desirable).
